sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate for the State of U.P./opposite party no.1 and perused the record.

By means of this application, the applicant has prayed for expeditious disposal of case being Case No. 34 of 2018 (State Vs. Hari Om @ Aashu and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 36 of 2017,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Hathras pending in the Court of Civil Judge (J.D.)/F.T.C. 2nd, Hathras within a time bound frame.
At the outset

sentences.text: 1 are husband and mother-in-law of daughter of the applicant are not appearing before the trial Court, therefore, the prayer of the applicant, who is complainant in this case, seeking direction to expedite the trial of the accused cannot be granted at this stage.

Learned counsel for the applicant does not dispute the aforesaid fact as pointed out by learned A.G.A. and in reply submits that the applicant may be permitted to withdraw this application with liberty to file the application afresh at the appropriate stage.
In view of the above, this Court finds force in the preliminary objection/submission of learned A.G.A. for the State that without appearance of accused before the trial Court, no direction to expedite the trial of the accused within time bound period can be issued.
However, having regard to the statement given by learned counsel for the applicant at the bar, this application is dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the applicant to file the application afresh at the appropriate stage, after appearance of accused before the trial Court.
Office is directed to return the certified copy of the documents, if any, to counsel for the applicant after retaining the photostat copy of the same on record as per rules.
Order Date :- 19.7.2023
